skills.name: Sine, cosine and tangent of an acute angle; complementary angles

note.text:
In a right-angled triangle, name the sides from the marked angle θ: the hypotenuse (longest), the opposite side (facing θ) and the adjacent side (next to θ, not the hypotenuse).
• sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse
• cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse
• tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent
Memory aid: SOH CAH TOA.
Complementary angles add to 90°: sin θ = cos(90° − θ) and cos θ = sin(90° − θ). For example sin 40° = cos 50°.

sections.heading: Naming the sides from the angle
Three ratios
sections.text:
For a given angle, the ratios of the sides are always the same, however big the triangle:
• sin θ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse
• cos θ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse
• tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent
Remember SOH CAH TOA. In the triangle with sides {3}, {4}, {5} and θ opposite the side {3}: sin θ = {frac(3, 5)}, cos θ = {frac(4, 5)}, tan θ = {frac(3, 4)}.
sin and cos are always less than {1}, because the hypotenuse is the longest side.

sections.heading: Complementary angles
sections.text:
The two acute angles of a right-angled triangle add up to {90}°: they are complementary.
The side opposite one is adjacent to the other. So sin θ = cos({90}° − θ) and cos θ = sin({90}° − θ).
For example sin {30}° = cos {60}° = {0.5}, and cos {20}° = sin {70}°.

misconceptions.explain: sin and cos of the same angle are equal only at {45}°.
The complement turns sine into cosine: sin θ = cos({90}° − θ).
The complement turns cosine into sine: cos θ = sin({90}° − θ).

solution: The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complement. So: {answer}.

misconceptions.explain: That is sin {A}°. Use sin({90}° − θ) = cos θ.

solution: {A}° and {90 - A}° add to {90}°: they are complementary.
sin({90} − θ) = cos θ, so sin {90 - A}° = cos {A}° ≈ {answer}.
